title: 503 Root-Cause and Scheduler Latency Diagnostic

cloud_metrics.direct_probe_attempt: invalid tunnel path and a separate kubectl jsonpath quoting error; no valid direct latency number retained

direct_probe_diagnostics.interpretation: Edge metrics over the KubeEdge tunnel is the dominant measurable probe cost. Edge health RTT is small. The 2-second metrics cache is already enabled in the live scheduler; observed faster scheduler calls are consistent with cache hits, while refreshes incur roughly one second.

edge_pressure_reproduction.edge_pressure_method: Two bounded CPU worker processes on Edge EC2 for approximately 60 seconds

errors.reason: target=queue; Edge CPU 100% > 75%; Cloud offload not viable because measured network latency was 233.1ms > 200ms
target=queue; Edge CPU 100% > 70%; Cloud offload not viable because measured network latency was 267.6ms > 200ms
target=queue; Edge CPU 100% > 75%; Cloud offload not viable because measured network latency was 252.3ms > 200ms
target=queue; Edge CPU 100% > 70%; Cloud offload not viable because measured network latency was 236.5ms > 200ms

edge_pressure_reproduction.confirmed_503_semantics: All four reproduced HTTP 503 responses were intentional QUEUE decisions from the placement policy, not demonstrated scheduler crashes, inference failures, or pod failures.

root_cause.primary_503_cause: When Edge CPU is overloaded and measured Edge-to-Cloud health RTT exceeds the 200ms policy limit, Low and Medium priority workloads are assigned QUEUE. The orchestrator maps non-edge/non-cloud targets to HTTP 503 with a clear detail string.
root_cause.high_priority_behavior: High priority is allowed to remain on Edge as best effort under poor network conditions, or to offload when Cloud is viable.
root_cause.latency_bottleneck: Edge /metrics fetch through KubeEdge is approximately 1.01 seconds on the measured host-side path. Health RTT is approximately 9ms. The scheduler already has a 2-second metrics TTL cache configured.
root_cause.prior_O5_11_caveat: O5.11 did not retain its five HTTP 503 bodies. This reproduction establishes the policy-generated 503 mechanism under the same overload/network-constrained condition, but does not prove every O5.11 response had the same reason.

limitations: The baseline and pressure phases are diagnostic samples, not a large-scale throughput benchmark.
The cloud metrics direct latency attempt was invalid and is explicitly excluded.
The Edge metrics direct timings were measured from the Cloud EC2 host through its local tunnel; scheduler logs independently confirm the same KubeEdge route is used by the scheduler.
The exact five O5.11 HTTP 503 bodies remain unavailable.
No code or deployment change was made in O5.12.
